entities.name: Caroline
entities.description: Caroline, a transgender woman and Melanie's close friend. Originally from Sweden, she moved away from her home country about four years before June 2023 and began transitioning around 2020. She paints, draws and makes stained glass, plays acoustic guitar, volunteers and mentors in the LGBTQ+ community, is pursuing a career in counselling and mental health, and is adopting as a single parent — she passed the adoption agency interviews on 20 October 2023. She keeps a guinea pig called Oscar.

entities.name: Melanie
entities.description: Melanie, Caroline's close friend: a married mother of at least three children, including a son hurt in a car accident in October 2023 and a youngest daughter whose first steps she treasures. She paints, took up pottery in July 2023 and paused it after an injury in September 2023, runs, plays the clarinet, and camps and hikes with her family. She married in about 2018 and has been making art for about seven years as of 2023.

entities.name: Melanie's husband
entities.description: Melanie's husband, married to her since about 2018 and father of her children. Melanie said the best part of her wedding day was marrying him and promising to be together forever.

entities.name: Amy Ellis Nutt
entities.description: Amy Ellis Nutt, author of Becoming Nicole, the book Caroline names as the one that guided her most.

entities.name: Oliver
entities.description: Oliver, Melanie's black dog, who once hid a bone in her slipper; one of the household's pets alongside the cat Luna and, from August 2023, the cat Bailey.

entities.name: Luna
entities.description: Luna, Melanie's cat, one of the household's pets alongside the dog Oliver; a second cat, Bailey, arrived by August 2023.

entities.name: Sweden
entities.description: Sweden, Caroline's home country, where her grandmother gave her the cross-and-heart necklace she treasures. Caroline moved away about four years before June 2023.

entities.name: LGBTQ support group
entities.description: The LGBTQ support group Caroline attended on 7 May 2023. The transgender stories told there inspired her, and she said it made her feel accepted and gave her the courage to embrace herself.

entities.name: Caroline's adoption agency
entities.description: The adoption agency Caroline chose, picked because it helps LGBTQ+ people adopt and for its inclusivity and support. She was looking into it in May 2023, applied in the week of 21 August 2023 and passed its interviews on 20 October 2023.

entities.name: Melanie's pottery class
entities.description: The pottery class Melanie signed up for on 2 July 2023, where she made a black-and-white flower-design bowl, a colourfully patterned bowl and a flower-decorated plate.

entities.name: Caroline's gender transition
entities.description: Caroline's gender transition, begun about three years before June 2023. Friends, family and mentors supported her throughout; it cost her a few friendships and left the rest more genuine, it is the subject of much of her art, and from June 2023 she spoke about it publicly.

entities.name: Caroline's adoption
entities.description: Caroline's plan to adopt as a single parent: researching agencies in May 2023, an adoption council meeting on 14 July 2023, applying to agencies in the week of 21 August 2023, contacting her mentor for advice on 13 October and passing the agency interviews on 20 October 2023.

entities.name: Caroline's counselling career plan
entities.description: Caroline's plan to work in counselling and mental health, first raised in May 2023 and narrowed by June 2023 to supporting trans people with self-acceptance and mental health. It grew out of her own mental health struggles and the support she received.

entities.name: Painting
entities.description: Painting, which both women practise. Melanie paints landscapes, still lifes, animals and nature scenes, often with her children, and turned to it while injured; Caroline has made art since she was about 17 and uses painting and drawing to express her trans experience and explore her identity, moving into abstract work by October 2023.

entities.name: Pottery
entities.description: Pottery, Melanie's craft from July 2023, which she calls therapy and a huge part of her life rather than a hobby; she had to stop after an injury in September 2023. Caroline had still not tried it as of September 2023 but was open to it.

entities.name: Running
entities.description: Running, one of Melanie's daily self-care practices. She ran a charity race for mental health on 20 May 2023 and by July 2023 was running longer distances to de-stress and clear her mind.

entities.name: Reading
entities.description: Reading, valued by both women: one of Melanie's daily me-time activities and what she turned to while injured in autumn 2023, and for Caroline a source of guidance — she is assembling a children's library for the family she hopes to adopt.

entities.name: Camping
entities.description: Camping, Melanie's family's summer tradition: the mountains in June 2023, the beach, the forest and more, with marshmallows and stories round the campfire. Their best memory is the Perseid meteor shower on the 2022 trip.

entities.name: Hiking
entities.description: Hiking, done by Melanie's family in the mountains and forests and by Caroline, whose hike in mid-August 2023 brought a confrontation with a group of religious conservatives that she later apologised for.

entities.name: LGBTQ advocacy
entities.description: Caroline's LGBTQ advocacy: a support group, a school talk, youth-centre volunteering, pride parades, an LGBTQ conference, a transgender poetry reading, mentoring LGBTQ youth, the activist group Connected LGBTQ Activists, and art made to speak for the trans community.

entities.name: Caroline's grandmother's necklace
entities.description: The cross-and-heart necklace Caroline's grandmother in Sweden gave her when she was young. It stands for love, faith and strength and reminds her of her roots and her family's support.

entities.name: Caroline's hand-painted bowl
entities.description: The hand-painted bowl a friend made for Caroline's 18th birthday, about ten years before June 2023; its pattern and colours remind her of art and self-expression.

entities.name: Becoming Nicole
entities.description: Becoming Nicole by Amy Ellis Nutt, the true story of a trans girl and her family. Caroline's favourite guiding book: it made her feel connected and hopeful and taught her self-acceptance and how to find support.

entities.name: Charlotte's Web
entities.description: Charlotte's Web, Melanie's favourite childhood book, which showed her how friendship and compassion can make a difference.

entities.name: Matt Patterson
entities.description: Matt Patterson, the musician whose concert Melanie took her family to on 13 August 2023 for her daughter's birthday; she praised his voice and songs.

entities.name: Oscar
entities.description: Oscar, Caroline's guinea pig, whose favourite food is parsley; Caroline first mentioned him on 23 August 2023.

entities.name: Bailey
entities.description: Bailey, the second cat in Melanie's household, mentioned on 23 August 2023 alongside the cat Luna and the dog Oliver.

entities.name: Connected LGBTQ Activists
entities.description: Connected LGBTQ Activists, the activist group Caroline joined on 18 July 2023. It is made up of all kinds of people investing in positive change, and holds regular meetings and plans events and campaigns.

entities.name: LGBTQ+ youth centre
entities.description: The LGBTQ+ youth centre Caroline visited and then volunteered at. A visit inspired her tree-and-sun painting in July 2023, and by August 2023 she was volunteering there regularly, sharing her story with the young people and helping organise a talent show for them in September 2023. Caroline calls it both 'a LGBTQ center' and 'an LGBTQ+ youth center'.

entities.name: LGBTQ youth mentorship programme
entities.description: The mentorship programme for LGBTQ youth Caroline joined on the weekend of 15–16 July 2023; through it she mentors a transgender teenager on building confidence and finding positive strategies.

entities.name: Caroline's LGBTQ art show
entities.description: The LGBTQ art show Caroline is putting together to exhibit her paintings alongside other LGBTQ artists, meant to spread understanding and acceptance. Planned in July 2023 for August, and by 25 August 2023 set for September 2023.

entities.name: Embracing Identity
entities.description: 'Embracing Identity', Caroline's painting of a woman standing for the journey of acceptance; she meant it to show warmth, love and self-acceptance, and showed it to Melanie on 14 August 2023.

entities.name: Sara Bareilles
entities.description: Sara Bareilles, singer of 'Brave', the song Caroline says holds the most significance for her.

entities.name: Ed Sheeran
entities.description: Ed Sheeran, singer of 'Perfect', which Melanie named among the modern music she likes.

entities.name: Grand Canyon
entities.description: The Grand Canyon, which Melanie's children enjoyed during the family road trip of the weekend of 14–15 October 2023 — the trip on which her son was in a car accident.

entities.name: Summer Sounds
entities.description: Summer Sounds, the band Melanie saw play an outdoor show before 28 August 2023; they played a pop song that got everyone dancing and singing.

entities.name: Playing the guitar
entities.description: Playing the acoustic guitar, which Caroline took up about five years before August 2023; it is how she gets her emotions out and escapes into them.

entities.name: Playing the clarinet
entities.description: Playing the clarinet, which Melanie started when she was young and uses to express herself and relax.

entities.name: Brave
entities.description: 'Brave' by Sara Bareilles, the song that means the most to Caroline: it is about being courageous and fighting for what is right, and hearing it makes her think about the paths she has taken and the progress she has made.

entities.name: Perfect
entities.description: 'Perfect' by Ed Sheeran, named by Melanie among the modern music she likes alongside classical composers such as Bach and Mozart.

claims.text: Melanie said on 17 August 2023 that she has always felt a strong connection to art and that it is both a sanctuary and a source of comfort that brings her happiness and fulfilment.
claims.speaker: Melanie

claims.text: Caroline and Melanie told each other on 17 August 2023 that holding on to what makes them happy is what keeps them going, and that they are glad of each other's friendship.
claims.speaker: Caroline

claims.text: Caroline and Melanie went to a Pride festival together with a group of friends in 2022 and both remember it as a blast.
claims.speaker: Caroline

claims.text: Caroline and Melanie agreed on 17 August 2023 to plan something special together in summer 2023 — either a family outing or a trip in nature for the two of them.
claims.speaker: Caroline

claims.text: Caroline applied to adoption agencies in the week of 21 August 2023, her first step towards becoming a mother, with a great deal of help from an adoption advice group she attended.
claims.speaker: Caroline

claims.text: Caroline said on 23 August 2023 that applying to adopt felt exciting but nerve-wracking, because parenting is such a big responsibility.
claims.speaker: Caroline

claims.text: Caroline keeps a guinea pig called Oscar, who she said on 23 August 2023 had been great company.
claims.speaker: Caroline

claims.text: Melanie's household gained a second cat, Bailey, by 23 August 2023, joining the cat Luna and the dog Oliver.
claims.speaker: Melanie

claims.text: Oscar the guinea pig's favourite food is parsley, and Caroline shared a photo of him eating it on 23 August 2023.
claims.speaker: Caroline

claims.text: Melanie's dog Oliver once hid a bone in her slipper, and Melanie has fed a horse a carrot.
claims.speaker: Melanie

claims.text: Caroline went horseback riding with her father through the fields as a child and has loved horses ever since.
claims.speaker: Caroline

claims.text: Melanie painted a horse on a wooden wall shortly before 23 August 2023 and said she loves painting animals because it is peaceful and horses have such grace.
claims.speaker: Melanie

claims.text: Caroline painted a self-portrait of a woman with a blue face in the week before 23 August 2023.
claims.speaker: Caroline

claims.text: Caroline felt liberated and empowered while painting her August 2023 self-portrait, and said painting helps her explore her identity, be true to herself and is therapeutic.
claims.speaker: Caroline

claims.text: Caroline said on 23 August 2023 that art, supportive people, promoting LGBTQ rights and being true to herself all give her a sense of freedom, and that she wants to live authentically and help others do the same.
claims.speaker: Caroline

claims.text: Caroline apologised to the people she had the confrontation with on her hike, telling Melanie on 25 August 2023 that the incident had bothered her.
claims.speaker: Caroline

claims.text: Melanie made a flower-decorated plate in her pottery class on 24 August 2023 and said pottery is relaxing and creative.
claims.speaker: Melanie

claims.text: Caroline had not tried pottery as of 25 August 2023, having been busy painting.
claims.speaker: Caroline

claims.text: Caroline painted a sunset after visiting the beach in the week before 25 August 2023, wanting to capture how amazing and calming it was to watch the sun dip below the horizon.
claims.speaker: Caroline

claims.text: Melanie and her family volunteered at a homeless shelter on 24 August 2023; she found it hard to see how neglected some people are but felt they could make a difference.
claims.speaker: Melanie

claims.text: Caroline said on 25 August 2023 that finding a community where she is accepted, loved and supported is what made the difference for her when she transitioned and joined the transgender community.
claims.speaker: Caroline

claims.text: A rainbow flag mural with an eagle is meaningful to Caroline because the flag reflects the courage and strength of the trans community and the eagle symbolises freedom, pride and her own resilience.
claims.speaker: Caroline

claims.text: Caroline made a stained glass window for a local church showing how time changes lives, meant to express her own journey as a transgender woman and the idea that growth and change should be accepted; she called it a symbol of togetherness and wanted to make something like it again.
claims.speaker: Caroline

claims.text: Caroline photographed a rainbow sidewalk painted for Pride Month that she came across while walking in her neighbourhood, and said it showed that love and acceptance can be found even where you least expect them.
claims.speaker: Caroline

claims.text: Caroline said on 25 August 2023 that art lifts her mood and lets her show her feelings and freeze beautiful moments, and that drawing flowers is one of her favourite things.
claims.speaker: Caroline

claims.text: Melanie's favourite kinds of painting are landscapes and still life, and as of 25 August 2023 she was planning several autumn-inspired paintings.
claims.speaker: Melanie

claims.text: Caroline was putting together an LGBTQ art show for September 2023 to exhibit her paintings alongside other LGBTQ artists, meaning it to spread understanding and acceptance.
claims.speaker: Caroline

claims.text: Melanie took her children to a park on 27 August 2023 and enjoyed watching them explore and play outdoors.
claims.speaker: Melanie

claims.text: Caroline volunteered at an LGBTQ+ youth centre shortly before 28 August 2023 and found it gratifying to talk with young people like herself; it reminded her how essential kindness and support are.
claims.speaker: Caroline

claims.text: Caroline was struck by how strong the young people at the LGBTQ+ youth centre were despite their challenges, and shared her own story so they would know they are not alone — an experience that reminded her of her own past loneliness.
claims.speaker: Caroline

claims.text: Caroline intended as of 28 August 2023 to carry on volunteering at the LGBTQ+ youth centre, where she had made strong connections and which she called an important part of her life.
claims.speaker: Caroline

claims.text: Caroline and the LGBTQ+ youth centre were putting together a talent show for the young people for September 2023.
claims.speaker: Caroline

claims.text: Melanie went to an outdoor show by the band Summer Sounds, who played a pop song that got everyone dancing and singing; she said it reminded her how music brings people together.
claims.speaker: Melanie

claims.text: Caroline said on 28 August 2023 that playing and singing let her express herself and connect with others, and that she finds it cathartic and uplifting.
claims.speaker: Caroline

claims.text: Caroline mainly plays the guitar, which helps her get her emotions out.
claims.speaker: Caroline

claims.text: Caroline started playing acoustic guitar about five years before August 2023, as a way to express herself and escape into her emotions.
claims.speaker: Caroline

claims.text: 'Brave' by Sara Bareilles is the song that means the most to Caroline: it is about being courageous and fighting for what is right, and hearing it makes her think about the paths she has taken and the progress she has made.
claims.speaker: Caroline

claims.text: Melanie plays the clarinet, which she started when she was young and uses to express herself and relax.
claims.speaker: Melanie

claims.text: Melanie likes both classical music such as Bach and Mozart and modern music such as Ed Sheeran's 'Perfect'.
claims.speaker: Melanie

claims.text: Caroline went biking with her group of friends on the weekend of 9–10 September 2023 and found the day out refreshing.
claims.speaker: Caroline

claims.text: Melanie's family went camping a few weeks before 13 September 2023, exploring the forest and hiking.
claims.speaker: Melanie

claims.text: Melanie said on 13 September 2023 that watching her children get excited about learning something new in nature is what makes being a parent worth it, and that roasting marshmallows and sharing stories round the campfire make the best memories.
claims.speaker: Melanie

claims.text: Caroline said on 13 September 2023 that she is inspired by seeing her work make a difference for the LGBTQ+ community, and that the support of her friends, family and mentors keeps her making art.
claims.speaker: Caroline

claims.text: Caroline has been making art since she was about 17, finding it empowering and cathartic and a way to show things that are hard to put into words.
claims.speaker: Caroline

claims.text: Melanie has been making art for seven years as of September 2023 and has settled on painting and pottery as her forms, finding both calming and satisfying.
claims.speaker: Melanie

claims.text: Painting and drawing helped Caroline express her feelings and explore her gender identity, and were important to her during her transition because they helped her understand and accept herself.
claims.speaker: Caroline

claims.text: Caroline had still not tried pottery as of 13 September 2023 but said she was game to try new art forms and might take it up.
claims.speaker: Caroline

claims.text: Caroline painted a red and blue piece representing her path as a trans woman: the two colours stand for the binary gender system and their mixing for smashing that rigid thinking, and she called it a reminder to love her authentic self.
claims.speaker: Caroline

claims.text: Caroline's transition changed her relationships: some close friends kept supporting her while a few could not handle it, and she said on 13 September 2023 that she is much happier among people who accept her and that her relationships now feel more genuine.
claims.speaker: Caroline

claims.text: Melanie had a good time at a café on the weekend of 9–10 September 2023, where a sign she photographed turned out to be only a precaution.
claims.speaker: Melanie

claims.text: Caroline contacted her mentor for adoption advice on 13 October 2023, saying she was ready to be a mother and share her love and a family.
claims.speaker: Caroline

claims.text: A friend of Melanie's adopted a child in 2022 after a long process and is now very happy, which made Melanie think she might adopt too.
claims.speaker: Melanie

claims.text: Caroline advised Melanie on 13 October 2023 to research and find an adoption agency or lawyer, gather references, financial information and medical checks, and prepare emotionally because the wait can be hard.
claims.speaker: Caroline

claims.text: Melanie was injured in September 2023 and had to take a break from pottery, which she uses for self-expression and peace.
claims.speaker: Melanie

claims.text: While off pottery Melanie kept busy reading the book Caroline had recommended and painting.
claims.speaker: Melanie

claims.text: Melanie painted a sunset with a pink sky in the week before 13 October 2023 because the colours made her feel calm.
claims.speaker: Melanie

claims.text: Caroline had been trying abstract painting as of October 2023, finding it freeing to put her feelings on the canvas without much of a plan.
claims.speaker: Caroline

claims.text: Melanie's abstract painting used peaceful blue streaks to convey tranquillity, because blue calms her; she wanted a serene mood with vibrant colours.
claims.speaker: Melanie

claims.text: Caroline attended a transgender poetry reading on 6 October 2023 where transgender people shared their stories through poetry; she found it a safe place for self-expression and empowering to hear others celebrate their identities.
claims.speaker: Caroline

claims.text: The energy, support and posters at the transgender poetry reading of 6 October 2023 inspired Caroline to make art.
claims.speaker: Caroline

claims.text: Caroline drew a woman in a dress standing for freedom and being real, as a reminder to stay true to herself and embrace her womanhood.
claims.speaker: Caroline

claims.text: Caroline and Melanie agreed on 13 October 2023 that being yourself is an ongoing adventure of learning and growing, and that they are glad to be on it together.
claims.speaker: Caroline

claims.text: Melanie's son was in a car accident during the family road trip on the weekend of 14–15 October 2023; he was unhurt, but Melanie and the family were badly frightened.
claims.speaker: Melanie

claims.text: Melanie said on 20 October 2023 that the accident reminded her that life is precious and made her think about how much she needs her family, and that her children had greatly enjoyed the Grand Canyon on the same trip.
claims.speaker: Melanie

claims.text: Melanie's other children were frightened by the October 2023 accident but were reassured that their brother would be all right, and she called them tough.
claims.speaker: Melanie

claims.text: Melanie said on 20 October 2023 that her children's resilience gives her the strength to keep going and that her family are her biggest motivation and support through hard times.
claims.speaker: Melanie

claims.text: Melanie and her children went on a nature walk on 19 October 2023, which the children loved and which was a relaxing way to wind down after the road trip.
claims.speaker: Melanie

claims.text: Melanie said on 20 October 2023 that camping with her family is a chance to be present together, bonding over stories, campfires and nature, and that waking to birdsong and fresh air refreshes her.
claims.speaker: Melanie

claims.text: Caroline passed the adoption agency interviews on 20 October 2023, a big move towards her goal of having a family.
claims.speaker: Caroline

claims.text: Caroline said on 22 October 2023 that she hopes to build her own family and give a home to children who have never had one, and that adoption is for her a way of giving back and showing love and acceptance.
claims.speaker: Caroline

claims.text: Caroline said on 22 October 2023 that finding self-acceptance was a long process and that she is now ready to offer love and support to those who need it.
claims.speaker: Caroline

claims.text: Caroline said transitioning and finding acceptance were both hard, and that the invaluable help of friends, family and people she looked up to carried her through and helped her find out who she really is — which is why she wants to pass that support on.
claims.speaker: Caroline

claims.text: Caroline and Melanie affirmed on 22 October 2023 that they will always be there for each other, and Caroline said the encouragement of those close to her made her who she is and that living honestly is freeing.
claims.speaker: Caroline

claims.text: Caroline's adoption went from researching agencies in May 2023, through an adoption council meeting on 14 July and applying to agencies in the week of 21 August, to contacting her mentor on 13 October and passing the adoption agency interviews on 20 October 2023.
claims.speaker: Caroline

claims.text: Caroline began transitioning around 2020 and by October 2023 said she was proud of who she is: supported throughout by friends, family and mentors, speaking publicly about her journey from June 2023, and working through her changing body and identity in painting and stained glass.
claims.speaker: Caroline

claims.text: Melanie's pottery went from signing up for a class on 2 July 2023, through a workshop with her children on 14 July and bowls and a plate made through August 2023, to a break forced by an injury in September 2023.
claims.speaker: Melanie

claims.text: Caroline has made art since she was about 17 and through 2023 used it to tell her trans story — a tree-and-sun painting in July, 'Embracing Identity' and a self-portrait in August, a stained glass window for a local church in August, a red-and-blue painting in September and abstract work by October — while preparing an LGBTQ art show of her paintings.
claims.speaker: Caroline
